name: Depot Dollars Expiring
goal: Get customers to spend their Depot Dollars before they expire by reminding them of the balance, showing small pieces it can go toward and explaining how to apply it at checkout.
trigger: Date-based: Klaviyo date-property trigger on the profile property depot_dollars_expiration_date. Hour 0 = the expiry date; messages go out 14, 3 and 2 days before it. Requires a Miva -> Klaviyo sync of depot_dollars_balance and depot_dollars_expiration_date. Until that sync exists, use the fallback: Klaviyo metric trigger Placed Order, with the first message 76 days after the order.
flow_filters: depot_dollars_balance > 0 (when synced). Klaviyo re-checks flow filters before every message, so a balance that is spent or expires stops the flow.
Placed Order zero times since starting this flow.
Fallback build only: no balance is available to filter on, so the Placed Order filter does the work. A newer order removes the profile from the older order's reminders and starts its own run.
exit_conditions: Places any order (flow filter). Post-Purchase takes over, and its E4 already says the new Depot Dollars are ready.
depot_dollars_balance drops to 0 because the balance was used or has expired.
The expiry date passes. E2, 2 days before, is the last message.
Unsubscribes from email: the email steps stop but S1 still sends if SMS-consented. Replies STOP: S1 is skipped but the emails still send.
smart_sending: Email on (16h) / SMS on (24h). This is the program default. DD ranks below Post-Purchase, Cart and Sample-to-Order, so if one of those sent within the window, this reminder gives way. If Smart Sending skips E2, SMS subscribers already got the date in S1.

branches.label: Everyone with an expiring balance
branches.rule: No split. The fallback build (Placed Order + 76 days) uses the no-balance alt versions of E1 and E2 and the fallback S1 text in build_notes.

kpis.metric: Placed order rate before expiry (per recipient)

kpis.metric: Share of expiring Depot Dollars redeemed before expiry
kpis.target: Set a baseline in the first 60 days, then +25%

build_notes: Data (required for the full build): sync two profile properties from Miva to Klaviyo at least daily, and again after every order, shipment and Depot Dollars redemption. (1) depot_dollars_expiration_date: the last day the soonest-expiring unspent Depot Dollars can be used, stored as a date. (2) depot_dollars_balance: the amount expiring on that date, formatted as currency with the dollar sign (e.g. $37.50). Every subject, SMS and headline assumes the token renders with the $ sign. Show the date in a readable format such as 'October 19'.

If Miva can only provide the total balance (not the amount expiring on the next date), tell the copy owner. For customers whose Depot Dollars come from more than one order, 'Your $X expires on [date]' would then overstate what is expiring, and the lines need to read 'Some of your $X in Depot Dollars expires on [date]'.

Trigger setup: a one-time Klaviyo date-property flow on depot_dollars_expiration_date (not set to repeat annually). Hour 0 = expiry date. DD-E1 goes out 14 days before at 10am local (offset_hours -336), DD-S1 3 days before at 11am local (-72) and DD-E2 2 days before at 10am local (-48). The profile qualifies again whenever the property moves to a new date after a later order.

Fallback until the sync exists: metric trigger Placed Order. E1 goes out 76 days after the order, S1 after 87 days and E2 after 88 days. Depot Dollars become available when the order ships and expire 90 days after they are earned, so the real expiry is on or after order date + 90 and fallback reminders arrive early, never late. Use the alt_versions of E1 and E2 (no balance or date tokens) and this S1 text: 'Architectural Depot: The Depot Dollars from your last order expire soon. Use them at checkout: {link} Reply STOP to opt out'.

Checkout mechanics: verify before launch. DD-E2 step 2 assumes the balance appears when the customer checks out signed in to the account that earned it, and step 3 assumes they apply it during checkout. Confirm with the Miva setup whether sign-in is required and whether Depot Dollars apply automatically or must be selected, then adjust steps 2 and 3 if needed.

The small-item cards (finials, plinth blocks, ceiling medallions, samples, shutter hardware) are ideas, not prices. Never show prices or 'free' language next to them, because balances vary and an item can cost more than the balance. Only the sample card links out, to the verified /BM-MAT-SAMPLE.html. Add category links for the other cards once their URLs are verified.

Priority: DD ranks below Post-Purchase, Cart and Sample-to-Order. Rely on Smart Sending for collisions and do not add 'not in flow X' filters here, because a flow filter would remove the profile from the rest of the reminder sequence.

SMS: DD-S1 goes out at 11am recipient local time, inside the 10am-8pm quiet-hours window, and counts toward the 3-per-rolling-7-days cap. With literal tokens the text is 160 characters. With a real balance and date it renders at about 125.
Images: use real Ekena product photography. The balance and date are always live HTML text and are never baked into an image.

steps.purpose: Make the balance feel real and easy to use. Many people forget they have Depot Dollars, or think they need a big project to use them. Show the amount and the date, then suggest small finishing pieces it can go toward.

blocks.title: How Depot Dollars work
blocks.text: Apply them during checkout. Each Depot Dollar is worth $1 off. They don't cover shipping, handling or tax, have no cash value and can't be transferred.

Saving up for something bigger, like [faux wood beams](https://www.architecturaldepot.com/faux-wood-beams.html) or a new mantel? Your Depot Dollars go toward any qualifying order placed by {{ depot_dollars_expiration_date }}.
